Subject: FinTechCo integration follow-up: API auth & key management

Hi Alice / Bob — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps on auth/key management so we can scope the integration session: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: server-to-server model inference for transaction enrichment and real-time fraud scoring (low-latency).
- No end-user sign-in required for the inference calls — calls originate from FinTechCo backend services.
- Regulatory requirement: keys must be rotated on a schedule and stored in a customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or HSM).
- Auditability: request-level logs and per-key usage breakdown desired for cost allocation.

Auth options we recommend for this pattern (pros/cons + where we usually land):
1) Service accounts with JWT (recommended for production):
   - Short-lived JWTs signed by FinTechCo's private key / integrated with your IdP (e.g., Okta) or using a workload identity.
   - Pros: no long-lived secrets inside the app, easier rotation, aligns with least-privilege.
   - Cons: requires minor setup (keypair + token exchange).

2) API keys with subkeys / scoped keys (recommended for dev & a simpler path):
   - Use environment-scoped API keys (dev/stage/prod) and rotate regularly.
   - Pros: minimal code changes, works immediately with our SDKs.
   - Cons: long-lived unless you implement short TTL subkeys; needs secure secret management.

3) OAuth (delegated) — less relevant unless calls need to be made on behalf of end users.

Key rotation & KMS integration notes:
- We support customer-managed keys via KMS integration for envelope encryption of persisted artifacts (e.g., caching of embeddings).
- For credential rotation we recommend: short-lived JWTs for prod; automatable API-key rotation via our Keys API for tooling/ops teams.
- We can ingest a public key for JWT verification or support OIDC/JWKS endpoints for token validation.

Next steps (proposed):
- Send a short architecture diagram and a sample service-account config (attached).
- Schedule a 60-minute architecture session next week to walk through token exchange flow, routing, and embedding storage. Can you share who on your side will own key rotation (ops/security) and whether you require HSM-backed signing?
- I'll also loop in David (runtime/integration) and Rishi (security/compliance) for the session.

Attachments: fintechco-integration-arch-diagram.png (diagram), sample-service-account-config.yaml

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

1) Key ownership: our Platform Security team (cc'd via procurement alias for contracting) wants HSM-backed signing for any keys used in production. We use AWS KMS + CloudHSM.
2) Rotation: we have an internal policy of rotating keys every 30 days; prefer automated rotation APIs.
3) Service accounts: we like the JWT flow but want to confirm whether Redwood supports verifying tokens against our JWKS endpoint (yes/no) and whether you can accept OIDC-issued tokens from Okta.
4) Per-route scoping: can we generate multiple keys/subkeys per environment so we can limit access by route (embeddings vs. generation)?

Would love a short architecture session on Wed 2/25 or Thu 2/26. Can you confirm availability and the right Redwood attendees?

Thanks,

Alice — thanks for the quick notes and the constraints. Wed 2/25 10:00am PT works for us — invite sent. Attendees from Redwood: Marissa (AE), David (Integration/Runtime), Rishi (Security), Aisha (DevX).

Quick answers to your questions ahead of the call:
- JWKS/OIDC: yes, we can verify tokens against your JWKS endpoint and accept Okta-issued OIDC tokens for service accounts. We'll include the verification flow in the diagram.
- HSM/KMS: we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS + CloudHSM acceptable). For signing keys you can either provide a public key for verification or integrate via an HSM-backed signing service; we'll document both paths.
- Per-route scoping: supported. We can enforce scopes in the token (recommended) or at the gateway (if you prefer central proxy enforcement). Token claims give better fine-grained auditability.

Attachments included: fintechco-integration-arch-diagram.png, sample-service-account-config.yaml, redwood-sow-draft.docx

See you Wed.
